name: Adjacent Segment Disease after Spinal Fusion
tags: adjacent segment disease after spinal fusion
definition: Symptomatic degeneration, stenosis, instability or deformity developing adjacent to a prior spinal fusion and producing new clinical symptoms.

typical: New axial pain after prior fusion

investigations.principle: Standing radiographs plus MRI/CT are selected to assess adjacent degeneration, fusion status and neural compression.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, occult injury, postoperative or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

green: Rehabilitation and symptom-directed care when stable
amber: Revision surgery is considered only when symptoms correlate with structural pathology.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Postoperative Kati/Prishtha phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Symptomatic degeneration, stenosis, instability or deformity developing adjacent to a prior spinal fusion and producing new clinical symptoms.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, respiratory distress, progressive neurological deficit, open injury, severe deformity, infection or other listed red flags.
